description: Two rules that no real terraform_data run can tell apart, because every one of its resources finishes in zero seconds. stage.alpha: three members, overlapping, and the node is busy from the FIRST start to the LAST finish — 10:00:00 to 10:02:02 is 122 seconds, not the 128 you get by adding them up and not the 120 the longest one took. stage.slow: the member that ran five minutes carries no identifier, so the node shows the one that ran ten seconds and does carry one — the identifier is taken from the longest member THAT HAS ONE, and nothing is enriched to produce a better answer. The phase span is the same rule one level up and cannot be computed on the page at all: a node reports its DURATION and not its boundaries, and durations of overlapping things do not add up. stage.alpha and stage.slow together run 10:00:00 to 10:05:00 — 300 seconds, not the 422 you get by adding the two node durations.
